name: PRBench
description: PRBench evaluates AI agents on end-to-end reproduction of computational results from published physics research papers. Agents receive only a paper and a task instruction, then must understand the methodology, implement algorithms from scratch, execute simulations, and produce quantitative outputs matching the original publication. It spans 30 expert-curated tasks across 11 subfields of physics, contributed and validated by over 20 research groups at Peking University.
typical_sota_score: 34% overall (OpenAI Codex / GPT-5.3-Codex); 0% end-to-end callback rate across all agents
reputation: Very new (March 2026); not yet widely adopted, but notable for its rigorous expert-validated design and stark findings around the gap between AI comprehension and execution in scientific contexts.
notes: Very small dataset (30 tasks), limiting statistical power. Tasks are physics-specific and may not generalize to other scientific domains. The benchmark is computationally expensive to run (sandboxed Docker environments, multi-hour execution budgets). Contamination risk is low given tasks are grounded in niche, expert-curated research papers. Agentified grading introduces its own potential failure modes. The 0% end-to-end callback rate suggests the benchmark is far from saturation.
